competitors.name: There's An AI For That (TAAFT)
competitors.how_astra_gallery_differs: TAAFT is a broad AI-tool directory; Astra Gallery is narrow to GPT-6 Astra builds/benchmarks and requires fetch-verified sources.

competitors.name: MyGPTs.dev
competitors.how_astra_gallery_differs: Custom-GPT discovery for ChatGPT; Astra Gallery catalogs demos, repos, and evals of one frontier model, not custom GPT wrappers.

competitors.name: AwesomeGPTs
competitors.how_astra_gallery_differs: Searchable GPT Store-style catalog at scale; Astra Gallery prioritizes 18–25 verified builds with proof_type and cost_note over volume.

competitors.name: ChatGPT App Directory
competitors.how_astra_gallery_differs: Official in-product apps/MCP integrations; Astra Gallery is an independent evidence gallery of what people actually built/measured with Astra.

competitors.name: Latent Space / AINews digests
competitors.how_astra_gallery_differs: Excellent narrative digests; Astra Gallery turns those signals into structured, filterable, re-verified seed cards with categories.

domain_recommendation.rationale: Short, memorable, gallery-native TLD; astra-gallery.com is clearer for SEO/branding if .gallery unavailable; astragallery.dev signals indie/dev but reads less premium.

entries.title: GPT-6 Astra official launch
entries.description: OpenAI’s flagship announcement positioning Astra for computer use, coding, math/science, professional work, and cybersecurity, with staged rollout and API model id gpt-6-astra.
entries.author: OpenAI
entries.cost_note: API standard $10/M input, $50/M output; Fast mode 2× price
entries.why_included: Canonical product framing and claimed capability map every gallery entry should be checked against.

entries.title: OpenAI launch thread on X
entries.description: Official X announcement thread for GPT-6 Astra (status 2095595741528125780), the primary social launch artifact cited across early demos.
entries.author: @OpenAI
entries.why_included: Primary launch media many community demos remix; link resolves (HTTP 200) even when embeds vary.

entries.title: Blender → Unreal house walkthrough (Dimillian)
entries.description: Thomas Ricouard (@Dimillian) walks through Astra building the launch-blog house via Blender headless/Python, Cycles renders, UE5 export pipeline, and a 60 FPS walkable app.
entries.author: @Dimillian (Thomas Ricouard)
entries.why_included: Concrete end-to-end 3D production pipeline (plan → Blender → UE5 → interactive app), not just a still render.

entries.title: Architectural visualization with Astra
entries.description: OpenAI Developers writeup of designing Solace: floor plans, editable Blender geometry via bpy, lived-in props, Cycles camera tours, and interactive UE5 walkthrough with operable fixtures.
entries.author: OpenAI Developers / Thomas Ricouard
entries.why_included: Long-form reproducible workflow showing Astra as a spatial design agent across Blender and Unreal.

entries.title: Building games with Astra (Void Explorer)
entries.description: Codex + Astra build of Void Explorer: 2,048 star systems, procedural planets, continuous space-to-ground descent in Three.js/WebGPU, plus Sunwake and Hollowflux browser games.
entries.author: Thomas Ricouard
entries.why_included: Playable, inspectable multi-game build with architecture, testing harness, and Sites deploy loop.

entries.title: House photo → editable Blender reconstruction
entries.description: Tom Krcha (@tomkrcha) feeds Astra a house photo and gets a detailed Blender reconstruction with toys, appliances, and furniture, claimed tweakable and runnable at 60 FPS.
entries.author: @tomkrcha (via techAU)
entries.why_included: Image-to-editable-3D reconstruction is a distinct spatial capability beyond text-to-scene demos.

entries.title: Background computer use + parallel agents roundup
entries.description: techAU launch roundup covering async tool calling, mid-stream steering, background OS computer use (screenshots/DOM/controls), and early Blender/Unreal community demos.
entries.author: Jason Cartwright / techAU
entries.cost_note: Cites OSWorld ~40 min/task vs ~75 min prior
entries.why_included: Clear product explanation of background computer use and parallel sub-agents with linked early builds.

entries.title: Latent Space: AI engineer for <$6/hour
entries.description: swyx/Latent Space early-access writeup after 20B+ Astra tokens: fleets of subagents, run babysitting, personal Arena clones, and framing Astra as an automated AI engineer.
entries.author: Latent Space
entries.cost_note: ~$6/hr at 33 tok/s and $50/M output; Ultra fleets cost much more
entries.why_included: Rare high-token practical burn report with concrete agent-orchestration patterns and cost framing.

entries.title: Latent Space AINews Astra launch digest
entries.description: Dense day-after digest aggregating official claims, Artificial Analysis/ARC/Epoch/Perplexity/Cognition/Vals numbers, safety/monitorability debate, and rollout friction.
entries.author: Latent Space
entries.cost_note: Summarizes $10/$50 pricing and per-task vs per-token debate
entries.why_included: Best single secondary index of verified third-party numbers and skeptical takes for curators.

entries.title: ARC Prize: Astra on ARC-AGI-3
entries.description: ARC Prize reports Astra 62.7% ($26k) on Semi-Private with Standard harness and 99.9% (~$19k) with Provider Adapter; fewer actions than humans on 96% of levels; emergent symbolic DSL notes.
entries.author: ARC Prize
entries.cost_note: Standard max ~$26,098; Provider Adapter high ~$18,817; ~$360/game cited in related Chollet commentary
entries.why_included: Independent interactive-reasoning eval with harness caveats and action-efficiency analysis, not just a headline score.

entries.title: Artificial Analysis: Coding vs Intelligence split
entries.description: Independent lab finds Coding Agent Index 67 (≈Fable 5, cheaper/task) but Intelligence Index flat at 61 vs Sol; ~3× coding token efficiency; Intelligence Index ~75% more expensive per task after 2.5× price hike.
entries.author: Artificial Analysis
entries.cost_note: Price $10/$50 (2.5× Sol); coding Pareto cost leader; intelligence ~75% costlier/task at max
entries.why_included: Essential non-cheerleading cost/perf reality check that separates coding-agent wins from general-intelligence hype.

entries.title: HN thread on AA 'major gains' title
entries.description: Hacker News discussion of Artificial Analysis results; top critique notes Intelligence Index 61→61 despite 'major gains' framing, plus broader benchmark-trust debate.
entries.author: HN / NiekvdMaas et al.
entries.cost_note: Commenters note cost-per-task Pareto may be the real gain
entries.why_included: Documented skeptical community read that keeps the gallery honest about marketing vs charts.

entries.title: Epoch FrontierMath Erdős: 2/68 Lean solves
entries.description: Epoch AI’s Lean-verified open Erdős problem set: only Astra scored (3%), solving problems 74 and 126 within $300/72h; extra runs found 5/68 but burned >$220k compute.
entries.author: Epoch AI (Greg Burnham, Tom Adamczewski)
entries.cost_note: Benchmark: $218–$247 for the two solves; extra attempts >$220,000 total
entries.why_included: Transparent open-problem math eval with Lean verification and published budgets—rare substance over vibes.

entries.title: Vellum: every published Astra benchmark table
entries.description: Side-by-side walkthrough of OpenAI’s computer-use, professional, coding, academic, science, cyber, and alignment tables, including AutomationBench 41.4% and contested coding rows.
entries.author: Nicolas Zeeb / Vellum
entries.cost_note: Notes $10/$50 vs Sol $4/$20 and that efficiency offset is still sparsely evidenced
entries.why_included: Best organized third-party unpack of vendor tables, including losses (HLE tools) and professional-work gains.

entries.title: SRE-Bench binary reverse engineering
entries.description: OpenAI reports Astra solves 88.0% of SRE-Bench tasks in one attempt and 99.2% within four (vs Sol 55.9%/68.7%), measuring reverse engineering of binaries without source.
entries.author: OpenAI (via Vellum summary)
entries.cost_note: Latent Space also notes ValsAI commentary on pass@4 / custom harness caveats
entries.why_included: Concrete cyber capability number with attempt protocol; gallery-worthy because it is capability + harness-caveat.

entries.title: ExploitBench saturation + Critical cyber tier
entries.description: Astra is OpenAI’s first Critical cybersecurity model; ExploitBench 100% (vs Sol 78.5%); advanced cyber gated via Daybreak; evals found zero-days later disclosed to maintainers.
entries.author: eesel AI / OpenAI Preparedness framing
entries.why_included: Defines the gated cyber story that separates Astra from prior OpenAI releases.

entries.title: eesel: what it costs and the catch
entries.description: Practitioner writeup contrasting agentic/cyber jumps with flat AA Intelligence Index, $10/$50 pricing, Daybreak gating, and OpenAI’s admission that monitorability decreased vs Sol.
entries.author: Kurnia Kharisma Agung Samiadjie / eesel
entries.why_included: Honest cost + safety catch piece suitable as a skeptical gallery card, not cheerleading.

entries.title: Transformer: neuralese & CoT monitorability fears
entries.description: Explainer on recurrent-depth/'neuralese' concerns around Astra, Ryan Greenblatt’s warning, and Jakub Pachocki’s reply that computation depth stays within ~2× of GPT-4.
entries.author: Transformer News
entries.why_included: Best accessible critical safety card on why monitorability, not just capability, belongs in an Astra gallery.

entries.title: HN: OpenAI begins rolling out GPT-6 Astra
entries.description: Hacker News discussion of CNBC rollout coverage, including Brockman’s AGI-era comments, price-per-task framing, and cyber-gated staged release.
entries.author: Hacker News
entries.cost_note: Quotes Brockman: price per task is what matters
entries.why_included: Public skeptical/governance thread pairing capability claims with rollout and cyber caution.

entries.title: Perplexity WANDR research-agent win
entries.description: Perplexity reports Astra tops WANDR at score 0.682 and $11.98/task — 13.5% above Fable 5.1 at 6.1% lower cost (per Latent Space AINews aggregation of @perplexity_ai).
entries.author: Perplexity (@perplexity_ai) via Latent Space
entries.why_included: Independent research-workflow leaderboard with explicit cost-per-task — gallery gold for knowledge work.

entries.title: FrontierCode near-parity at lower cost
entries.description: Latent Space AINews summarizes Cognition: on FrontierCode 1.1 Astra is within 0.4 points of Fable 5 at ~64% lower cost; Vellum notes Extended 64.5% slightly trails Fable 5’s 64.9%.
entries.author: Cognition / Latent Space; cross-check Vellum
entries.cost_note: ~64% lower cost vs Fable 5 at near-parity (per @cognition summary)
entries.why_included: Mergeability-oriented coding eval showing economics, not just pass rates.

entries.title: OSWorld 2.0 faster desktop agency
entries.description: Vendor/third-party tables: Astra ~72.6% on OSWorld 2.0 at ~40 minutes/task versus Sol ~65.7% at ~75 minutes; ScreenSpot-Pro 92.7% vs 76.9%.
entries.author: OpenAI (via Vellum)
entries.cost_note: ~47% less time per OSWorld task vs Sol
entries.why_included: Quantifies the computer-use speed story that demos alone cannot prove.

entries.title: AutomationBench professional work jump
entries.description: OpenAI’s AutomationBench shows Astra 41.4% vs Fable 5.1 31.4% and Sol 18.1% on template-driven professional automation (slides/spreadsheets/analyses).
entries.author: OpenAI (via Vellum)
entries.why_included: Largest published professional-work delta; anchors docs/office category with numbers.

entries.title: FrontierMath Tier 4 saturation claim
entries.description: OpenAI reports Astra at 97.6% on FrontierMath Tier 4 (v2) vs Sol ~83% and Fable 5.1 87.8%; paired with claims of helping solve long-standing open math problems.
entries.author: OpenAI (via Vellum); Epoch notes funding caveats
entries.cost_note: Vellum notes Epoch: OpenAI funded FrontierMath and has exclusive access to part of it
entries.why_included: Headline math saturation number with an important independence caveat for gallery honesty.
